# Mac Life — German Mac review

- Original source: [Robin Hood – Die Legende von Sherwood](https://www.maclife.de/testcenter/spiele-und-edutainment/ab-12-jahre/robin-hood-%E2%80%93-die-legende-von-sherwood)
- Author / publication: Jürgen Beck, signature; erdmann_red, page byline; Mac Life.
- Language / date: German; 2005-04-02.
- Access: Full article and test-result table retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

The review describes the combination of tactical infiltration, camp preparation, and character cooperation. It praises detailed backgrounds, voice acting, and atmospheric music, while criticizing pixelated zoom, blind spots caused by the fixed viewpoint, and the visual mismatch of character portraits. Its German test grade is 1.9, labeled good.

The table records historical Mac requirements including a 300 MHz G3, Mac OS X 10.2, and 128 MB RAM. The article attributes lockpicking to Will Scarlet; retain that as a source discrepancy rather than adopting it as verified character documentation.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: kicker "Kommandos im Mittelalter"; title "Robin Hood – Die Legende von Sherwood"; page byline "Von erdmann_red", 02.04.2005 - 00:00 Uhr; article signed "Jürgen Beck" at the end of the body; test-result table with grade "1,9 gut" (German school-grade scale, 1 best); retrieved directly from maclife.de (page currently wrapped in Mac Life+ subscription promotion; copyright maclife.de 2026). German commercial review, not transcribed.

Lead: "Take from the rich and give to the poor" echoes from Nottingham's battlements; the player dons the tights and goes raiding in "a successful mix of tactics game and adventure".

Body, in order:

- Intro: the legend of the nobleman declared a criminal and stripped of his property while absent from England; countless books and films; now a game lets the player slip into Robin's skin to free the people from the cruel Sheriff of Nottingham.
- Section "Treffpunkt: Wald" (meeting point: forest): ingredients are a pinch of role-playing, a touch of adventure, and a lot of real-time strategy and tactics. The story does not deviate from the original. First the servant Stuteley leads the player into the forest, which serves as camp where followers rest after work, work on their abilities and re-equip. Then the famous archery contest, the meeting with Maid Marian, and battles in medieval towns follow. The next mission area is chosen on a strategic overview map; huge castles such as Nottingham and Leicester, or wooded roads, serve as raiding grounds.
- Section "Unschlagbares Team": the maps are lovingly designed and drawn in detail. Each character has special abilities to be used sensibly: Robin is perfect with the bow and knocks enemies out silently; Little John carries the unconscious aside; Will Scarlet is described as "a master at picking locks" (recorded as the article's claim).
- Stealth: never attract the attention of the numerous guards; caution is the top rule. Robin often needs a detour, e.g. distracting guards with an arrow shot so companions can cross a castle courtyard. The band hides in the many buildings, where useful extras and hints are often found.
- Combat: despite the secrecy it comes to fights "far too often". The player draws patterns with the mouse that the heroes convert into attacks; a circle, for example, produces a powerful all-round blow.
- Section "Mittelalterliche Pracht": the story is mostly told in "plain text passages", accompanied by great voice acting and atmospheric music. Splendid, detailed background graphics; mouse-wheel zoom is convenient but then shows only "pixel mush"; the rigid perspective creates some blind spots that make survival harder.
